md_name: Single Amplified Archaeal Genome Sequencing Workflow
md_description: Workflow for archaeal community samples from extreme environments, including physical sample handling, lysis, isothermal amplification, high-throughput sequencing, and downstream genome assembly. The DAG captures the data-generating pipeline used to study archaeal adaptation and ecosystem biochemistry in extreme habitats such as hydrothermal vents.

archaeal_community_sample.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the intrinsic identity and origin of the collected archaeal community sample, not any downstream lysis, amplification, sequencing, or computational outputs. I included fields for sample identity/provenance and the environmental context of collection because those are explicitly owned by the root sample entity and are required to interpret extreme-environment archaeal datasets. I excluded collection/handling protocol details, lysis method, kit specifications, instrument settings, file properties, and assembly outputs because those belong to Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no need to suppress overlaps with prior schema entries.

md_schema.descr: Unique sample identifier assigned to this archaeal community sample in the study metadata table; use a stable string identifier such as 'S01' or 'HVV-2024-003'. This is recorded once at the sample/entity level and links the collected material to all downstream workflow nodes.

Geographic and environmental origin of the collected archaeal community sample, describing the extreme habitat from which it was obtained (for example, hydrothermal vent, hot spring, deep-sea hydrothermal chimney, hypersaline basin). Record the site name or location string as used by the study.

Collection location for the sample as a human-readable string, including site name and, when available, coordinates or region name. Use this to indicate where the specimen was physically obtained before any processing.
Date the archaeal community sample was collected in the field or expedition, recorded at the time of sampling. Use ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) when possible.

Physical material collected for this sample, indicating the environmental matrix from which archaeal cells were obtained, such as water, sediment, biofilm, vent chimney surface, or microbial mat. This describes what the sample is, not how it was processed.

In situ temperature at the sampling point, measured in degrees Celsius at the time and place of collection. Typical extreme-habitat values may range from near 0 to >100 Celsius depending on the site; record the field measurement associated with the sample origin.

In situ pH measured at the sampling point during sample collection. Typical values may range from strongly acidic to strongly alkaline in extreme environments; record the field measurement closest to the sample origin.

In situ salinity or practical salinity units (PSU) measured at the sampling point during collection, when relevant for aquatic or brine-associated extreme sites. Use the value associated with the sample origin and field measurement.

In situ hydrostatic or ambient pressure at the sampling point, expressed in atmospheres. This is particularly relevant for deep-sea or subsurface extreme habitats and should reflect the collection environment.

Oxygen availability at the sampling site at the moment of collection, capturing the environmental redox context of the archaeal community sample. Choose the value that best matches the in situ condition.

Primary extreme environmental category describing the habitat of origin for this sample, used to group samples by collection context in the study. Select the category that best matches the site description.

cell_lysis.reasoning: This Process node should capture how cell disruption was performed, including protocol parameters and reagent/method details that define the lysis operation itself. I included only fields that describe the lysis method, operating conditions, and process-level outcome quality relevant to releasing genomic material. I excluded sample origin, DNA identity, amplification kit details, sequencing instrument settings, raw file properties, and assembly outputs because those belong to the Entity, downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated field list was provided here, so I avoided duplicates by staying strictly within the lysis process territory.

md_schema.descr: Primary cell disruption approach used for archaeal cell lysis in this step, recorded as the protocol method applied to the sample before DNA release. Choose the method category that best matches the actual lysis treatment used in the experiment.

Name of the key lysis reagent, buffer, enzyme, or kit component used to disrupt archaeal cells, if applicable. Record the reagent as stated in the protocol, such as SDS, lysozyme, proteinase K, bead-beating buffer, or a commercial lysis mix.

Concentration of the principal lysis reagent used during cell disruption, with units embedded in the value description as appropriate for the protocol (for example, mg/mL, % w/v, or U/mL). Record the concentration measured or prepared for this lysis step.

Temperature used during the lysis incubation step, in degrees Celsius. Record the actual process temperature applied to the sample during cell disruption, typically within room temperature to elevated incubation ranges depending on protocol.

Duration of the lysis treatment, measured in minutes from the start of the disruption step to completion. Typical values may range from a few minutes to several hours depending on the chosen lysis method.
Number of repeated lysis cycles applied during the disruption step, such as freeze-thaw rounds, bead-beating bursts, or incubation repeats. Record the total count of cycles used for this process.

Instrument or protocol intensity setting used to control lysis strength when applicable, such as bead-beating speed, vortex level, sonication power, or mixer setting. Record the setting as used in this specific lysis operation.

Process-level assessment of whether the lysis step successfully produced liberated genomic material suitable for downstream amplification. Use this as a qualitative outcome indicator for the lysis operation only, not a measure of final DNA yield or sequencing quality.

lysate_dna.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the post-lysis material itself: the liberated DNA lysate as an intermediate biological sample ready for amplification. I included fields for the lysate identity and intrinsic DNA-state properties that characterize what the material is at this stage, along with basic preparation state and concentration/volume information needed to use it downstream. I excluded lysis protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded amplification kit, sequencing, raw read, or assembly details because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so I focused on non-overlapping entity-level properties specific to the lysate.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for this post-lysis DNA lysate sample, used to track the intermediate material before amplification. Record a stable string such as 'L01' or 'lysate_HVV_003' as used in the study metadata.

Identifier of the upstream archaeal community sample from which this lysate was produced. Use the same sample identifier assigned at the root entity level to preserve traceability of the biological material.

State of the genomic material present in the lysate after lysis, describing whether the DNA is liberated, partially fragmented, or otherwise prepared for amplification. Record the condition of the nucleic acid material at the lysate stage.

Total recovered lysate volume available after cell lysis, measured in microliters at the time the sample is handed off to amplification. Typical values may range from single-digit to hundreds of microliters depending on preparation scale.

Concentration of DNA in the lysate, measured in nanograms per microliter at the point the post-lysis material is prepared for amplification. Use the concentration value determined by the study's quantification method if available.

Spectrophotometric DNA purity ratio A260/A280 for the lysate, measured when the post-lysis material is assessed prior to amplification. Typical DNA values are often around 1.8, with lower or higher values suggesting contamination or unusual composition.

Short description of how the lysate was held before amplification, capturing the material's preservation state as an entity property rather than a process parameter. Examples include 'on_ice', '4_celsius', '-20_celsius', '-80_celsius', or 'immediate_use'.

isothermal_amplification.reasoning: This Process node should capture how the DNA lysate was amplified, including the isothermal amplification chemistry, kit/protocol details, reaction setup, and process-level outcome. I included fields for kit identity, enzyme/polymerase, incubation settings, input amount, reaction volume, and a qualitative success indicator because these are operational parameters needed to reproduce the amplification step. I excluded sample provenance, lysate intrinsic properties, sequencing instrument settings, raw file properties, and assembled genome metrics because those belong to the Entity, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I avoided overlap by keeping the schema strictly within amplification-process territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the isothermal amplification kit or protocol used to amplify the lysate DNA in this process, recorded as stated by the study or manufacturer. Examples include commercial multiple displacement or whole-genome amplification kits used for archaeal DNA amplification.

Isothermal amplification chemistry used in this step, identifying the general protocol family applied to the lysate DNA. Choose the category that best describes the amplification mechanism used in the experiment.

Name of the DNA polymerase or key amplification enzyme used in the isothermal reaction, if specified by the kit or protocol. Record the enzyme as reported in the method, such as phi29 DNA polymerase or a proprietary enzyme mix.
Total isothermal amplification reaction volume, in microliters, prepared for this process step. Record the volume of the complete reaction mixture assembled before incubation.

Amount of lysate DNA input into the amplification reaction, measured in nanograms at the time the process was set up. Typical values may range from picograms to tens of nanograms depending on whole-genome amplification protocol.
Incubation temperature used for the isothermal amplification reaction, in degrees Celsius. Record the actual process temperature maintained throughout the amplification step.

Total incubation time for the isothermal amplification reaction, measured in minutes from reaction start to completion. Typical durations may range from tens of minutes to several hours depending on the kit and protocol.

Number of amplification rounds, incubation phases, or reaction cycles applied in the isothermal protocol, when the method uses repeated rounds rather than a single continuous incubation. Record the count used for this amplification step, or 0 if not applicable.

Process-level assessment of whether the amplification yielded sufficient DNA product for sequencing. Use this as a qualitative outcome indicator for the amplification operation only, not a measure of final sequencing quality or assembly completeness.

amplified_dna_library.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the amplified DNA product itself as a sequencing-ready library/intermediate material, not the amplification protocol or the sequencing capture session. I included fields that characterize the library’s identity, whether it is properly adapter-free or ready-for-loading, and the physical quantity/size profile needed to understand the material entering sequencing. I excluded amplification kit details and reaction conditions because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded sequencer model/settings and raw file properties because those belong to Capture and Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so I kept this schema limited to non-overlapping entity-level library properties.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified DNA library generated from the isothermal amplification step, used to track the sequencing-ready material. Record a stable string such as 'LIB01' or 'amplified_HVV_003'.
Identifier of the upstream DNA lysate from which this amplified library was produced. Use the lysate identifier assigned at the post-lysis entity level to preserve sample provenance.

General type of amplified DNA material prepared for sequencing, indicating the library's entity state before instrument loading. Use the category that best matches the product of the amplification workflow.
Concentration of the amplified DNA library measured before sequencing, in nanograms per microliter. Record the concentration used to normalize or load the library for sequencing.
Total mass of amplified DNA available in the library at the time it was prepared for sequencing, expressed in nanograms. This reflects the amount of material carried forward into the capture step.
Representative fragment size of the amplified DNA library, in base pairs, measured prior to sequencing. Use the modal, mean, or target size reported for the library prep if available.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 for the amplified DNA library, measured after amplification and before sequencing. Typical DNA libraries are often near 1.8; values far from this may indicate contamination.

Whether the amplified DNA library was accepted as ready for sequencing loading without additional upstream processing. This indicates the material state of the library entity rather than any sequencing instrument configuration.

high_throughput_sequencing.reasoning: This Capture node should capture the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to generate raw reads from the amplified library. I included fields for sequencer identity and configurable run settings such as chemistry, read length, run mode, and loading/input parameters because these are active instrument/session properties. I also included a run-level quality indicator because it belongs to the capture session and helps interpret the generated signal. I excluded sample provenance, library intrinsic properties, raw file format/path/size, and assembly or processing outputs because those belong to Entity, Signal, or downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I avoided overlap by restricting the schema to the sequencing capture territory only.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the high-throughput sequencing instrument used for this capture step, recorded as the hardware vendor name at the time of sequencing. Examples include Illumina, Oxford Nanopore, or Thermo Fisher.
Model name or platform designation of the sequencing instrument used to generate the raw reads, such as a specific benchtop or production sequencer model.
Instrument serial number for the sequencer used in this capture session, recorded as the hardware identifier on the instrument. Use the exact serial string if available, for example 'SN12345678'.

Sequencing technology used during the capture session, describing the instrument chemistry or platform family that generated the raw reads. Select the technology category that best matches the device configuration used.

Configured read length for the sequencing run, in base pairs for short-read platforms or the nominal read target used for the run. Record the instrument setting or intended output read length at capture time.
Operational mode of the sequencing run, describing whether the capture session was configured for single-end or paired-end acquisition, or another mode appropriate to the platform.
Identifier of the consumable used in the sequencing run, such as the flow cell, chip, or cartridge loaded for this capture session. Record the platform-specific consumable ID if available.

Library loading concentration or input amount used for the sequencing run, expressed in pmol when applicable to the platform. Record the value actually loaded onto the sequencer for this capture session.

Total duration of the sequencing capture session, measured in hours from run initiation to completion. Typical values vary by platform and chemistry, and should reflect the actual instrument run time.

Capture-level qualitative assessment of whether the sequencing session produced usable raw data with the expected yield and instrument behavior. Use this as a run outcome indicator only, not as a file-level quality metric.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw data artefact produced by sequencing: the read files themselves and their technical properties. I included fields for file identity, storage, format, basic size/dimension metrics, and raw-data quality indicators because these are properties of the signal artifact rather than the capture instrument or biological material. I excluded sequencer model/settings, sample provenance, library properties, and downstream filtering or assembly metrics because those belong to Capture, Entity, or downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so I kept the schema confined to non-overlapping raw-read file characteristics.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw sequence read file or file set generated by the sequencing run, used to track the signal artefact in the dataset. Use a stable string such as 'RR01' or a platform-specific file identifier.

Identifier of the sequencing capture session that produced this raw read file, linking the signal artefact back to the corresponding sequencing run. Use the capture/run identifier assigned in the sequencing step.
File format of the raw sequencing reads, describing the on-disk encoding of the signal artefact. Examples include FASTQ, BAM, or platform-specific raw read containers.

Storage location or path where the raw sequencing read file is kept in the dataset or repository, recorded as a string path or URI. Examples include local filesystem paths, object-store URIs, or accession-based storage references.

Size of the raw read file in bytes, measured for the stored artefact after sequencing. This is a technical property of the signal file and typically ranges from kilobytes to many gigabytes depending on run depth.
Number of reads contained in the raw sequencing file or file set, counted from the unprocessed signal output. This dimension metric reflects the total raw read yield before any filtering or trimming.
Total number of sequenced bases represented by the raw reads, measured in base pairs across the unprocessed file. This is a file-level dimension metric for the raw data artefact.

Technical quality flag for the raw sequence read file, indicating whether the file appears complete and readable at the signal level. Use this only for file integrity or obvious artefact issues, not for biological interpretation.

read_processing.reasoning: This Process node should capture the computational transformation applied to raw reads before assembly, including the software used and key filtering/trimming parameters. I included fields for software identity and version, repository, processing actions, and cutoffs because these describe how the raw signal was transformed. I also included a process-level quality indicator because it reflects whether the processing step succeeded and produced usable output. I excluded raw file properties, sequencer configuration, sample provenance, and assembly outputs because those belong to Signal, Capture, Entity, or downstream Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I avoided overlap by limiting the schema to read-processing operation details only.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to process the raw reads in this step, recorded as the computational agent that performed trimming, filtering, or related preprocessing. Examples include fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, or platform-specific pipelines.

Version of the read-processing software used in this step, recorded exactly as executed for reproducibility. Provide the version string from the run environment or pipeline configuration, such as '0.23.4'.

Repository or source location for the read-processing software or pipeline used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, release page, or package reference. Record where the exact computational tool implementation can be obtained.

List or short description of the preprocessing operations applied to the raw reads, such as adapter trimming, quality trimming, length filtering, or contaminant removal. Record the actions that were actually performed in this processing step.
Phred quality score threshold used to trim or filter reads during preprocessing, if applicable. Typical values may range from 10 to 40 depending on the pipeline and sequencing platform.
Minimum read length retained after processing, in base pairs. Reads shorter than this cutoff were discarded or clipped during the preprocessing step.
Adapter sequence used as the target for trimming, if adapter removal was performed. Record the adapter sequence or adapter name applied during read processing.

Process-level assessment of whether the read-processing step produced usable cleaned reads suitable for assembly. Use this as an operational outcome indicator for the preprocessing step only, not as a measure of assembly quality.

processed_reads.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the processed-read artefact itself, but I had to remove fields that collided with previously generated DAG-wide field names. To avoid repeating file-level schema already used for earlier signal nodes, I retained only non-colliding processed-read properties that still characterize the cleaned reads and their suitability for assembly. I excluded processing software, trimming settings, and assembly outputs because they belong to other node types, and I also omitted the colliding generic file-format/path/size/read-count fields per the DAG-wide uniqueness constraint. The remaining fields focus on processed-read identity, provenance, read-length summary, and technical suitability.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the processed read file or file set produced after read cleaning and filtering, used to track the signal artefact prepared for assembly. Use a stable string such as 'PR01' or a repository-specific processed-read ID.

Identifier of the upstream raw read file that was transformed into this processed read artefact. Use the raw read file identifier assigned at the signal level to preserve provenance through preprocessing.
Average read length of the processed read set, measured in base pairs after trimming and filtering. This summary statistic characterizes the cleaned reads that will enter genome assembly.

Technical quality flag for the processed read file, indicating whether the cleaned read set is complete and suitable for downstream assembly. Use this only for file-level integrity or suitability, not for biological interpretation.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This Process node should capture the computational assembly operation itself: the software agent, assembly strategy, and key run parameters used to transform processed reads into contigs. I excluded raw/processed read file properties and the generic file fields that previously collided across the DAG, because those belong to Signal nodes and are not appropriate here. I also excluded sample provenance, sequencing capture settings, and final assembly object properties because those belong to Entity, Capture, or the downstream Derivative node. Since no already_generated list was provided in this turn, I selected assembly-specific process fields and kept names distinct from prior signal metadata.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used in this process step, recorded as the computational agent that assembled the processed reads into contigs. Examples include SPAdes, MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes, or other assembly tools used for archaeal genome reconstruction.

Version of the genome assembly software used in this step, recorded exactly as executed for reproducibility. Provide the version string from the run environment or workflow configuration, such as '3.15.5'.

Repository or source location for the assembly software or pipeline implementation used in this step, such as a GitHub URL, release page, or package reference. Record where the exact computational tool can be obtained.

Assembly strategy or mode used to reconstruct the archaeal genome from processed reads, describing the algorithmic approach applied in this process. Choose the category that best matches the actual run configuration.

K-mer sizes used by the assembler, if applicable, recorded as the set or comma-separated list of integer k values configured for the assembly run. These are the explicit assembly parameters used to build contigs from the processed reads.
Minimum contig length cutoff used during assembly output filtering, in base pairs. Contigs shorter than this threshold were excluded from the assembly process output.
Number of CPU threads allocated to the assembly software during this process step, recorded as the compute configuration used for the run.

Process-level assessment of whether the assembly run produced a usable draft contig set suitable for downstream interpretation. Use this as an operational outcome indicator for the assembly step only, not as a description of the contigs themselves.

archaeal_genome_assembly.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed genome assembly result itself, not the upstream assembly software or the input read files. I included fields that characterize the derived contig set and its scientific quality/interpretability, such as assembly identity, contig statistics, completeness/contamination, and binning/taxonomic context. I excluded processing and capture parameters, raw/processed read file properties, and sample provenance because those belong to upstream nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I limited the schema to derivative-specific output properties needed to understand and reuse the assembled archaeal genome.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived archaeal genome assembly, used to track the computed contig set produced by genome assembly. Record a stable string such as 'ASM01' or 'archaea_assembly_HVV_003'.

Identifier of the processed read file used as input to this genome assembly, preserving provenance from the upstream signal artefact. Use the processed-read identifier assigned at the preprocessing stage.

Number of contigs present in the final draft archaeal genome assembly, counted in the derived contig set after assembly and any output filtering. This is a basic size descriptor of the computed result.

Total length of all contigs in the draft genome assembly, measured in base pairs. Typical archaeal draft assemblies may span hundreds of kilobases to several megabases depending on completeness and coverage.
Length of the largest contig in the derived genome assembly, measured in base pairs. This provides a simple indicator of contiguity for the assembled archaeal genome.
N50 contig length for the derived assembly, measured in base pairs. This summary statistic describes assembly contiguity and is calculated from the final contig set.

Estimated genome completeness of the derived archaeal assembly, expressed as a percentage from 0 to 100. Record the post-assembly quality estimate used to judge how much of the expected genome is represented.

Estimated contamination or mixed-genome fraction in the derived archaeal assembly, expressed as a percentage from 0 to 100. This quality metric is assessed on the computed assembly and helps interpret genome purity.

Taxonomic assignment inferred for the derived archaeal genome assembly, reported at the most appropriate level supported by the analysis. Use a string such as a genus, family, or higher archaeal lineage label when available.

Short scientific summary of the adaptive or ecological interpretation supported by the derived assembly, such as evidence for heat tolerance, sulfur metabolism, or other extreme-environment adaptations. This is a concise result-level descriptor of the computed genome product.
